title: Slipping from No. 1: new personalities and three different bands
summary: Salazar suggests the billing rivalry hurt; Machito says audiences like new personalities, compares Glenn Miller and boxers, and says his band was the architect.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Okay. In 1952,'53 I notice, and is my own observation, that the Machito band slipped from No. 1 to

about No. 3. It didn't lose any quality, in fact, it was getting better and better, because those Tico recordings and Continental recordings that weren't on the Tico label, were great and they sold. The proof is "El Jamaiquino", "Minoso al Bate", the cha cha cha recordings of "La Paella" and "Sopa de Pichon", "Quimbombo", "El Niche", these became monsters and these are the ones that the dancers wanted to hear at the Palladium. Now, even though these recordings were just as good and danceable as the great things that Tito Puente and Tito Rodriguez put out at the same time, your band didn't get the exposure that those two guys were getting; because they were like rivals. Don't you think that that rivalry between them and that top-billing issue hurt you, because of the attention that they got fighting for the top line?

Is possible, but I don't think so. Is possible, but I don't think so. It's just a matter -- ahhh People liked new personalities. You could be the best -- it's like in fighting, in boxing; a new personality. You see now all the talk about Duran and Leonard. Leonard is a new personality. Duran is a great fighter, he was considered the best in this decade. It must be a reason why. It wasn't me or my wife that say that he is a good fighter, no, the connoisseur, the greatest people in the sport business consider Duran a great fighter. So in music is the same. I remember when Glenn Miller come about. The people was saying that Glenn Miller was the greatest band in the world

without respect the opinion of everybody that was listening to the band. But what about Benny Goodman, what about Artie Shaw? They was good bands too, top bands. But he come back with a new sound, a very understandable sound, and he just got the attention of the people.
If I understand you right, then what you are saying is that you had three different bands here. They all sound different and each has its following?

Okay. I agree with you because I like all three of you, but the Machito orchestra happened to be my sentimental favorite. But, you know, Tito Puente just overwhelmed me at that time and then there were things that Tito Rodruguez did that overwhelmed me, but the Machito band has been consistent since 1941 and, you know, this is something that never left my mind. So then it's your honest opinion that even though you gave in to Puente and Rodriguez on the billing issue, it never hurt you then.
No, no. It's just a matter of ----
You didn't do it because you wanted to keep their friendship, you did it because you really believed it wouldn't hurt you monetarily or any other way.

No, it just is another thing. Ahh - a family man have three, four children and is always somebody that had all the privileges for one reason or other, and one son is a lawyer, the other one is an architect and the third one is a pharmacist. The two career, a lawyer and the

architect, is more difficult to be architect than to be a pharmacist; two year you can't compare with an architect, with algebra and geometry and trigonometry, all those complications; so an architect when he make a mistake, forget it!!! (chuckle)
